title: Faqir manifest
description: The machine-readable contract shipped beside every Faqir component and theme. A file validates as either a component manifest (`<name>.manifest.json`) or a theme manifest (`<name>.theme.json`). The PROTOCOL it describes is FROZEN at 1.0: until 2.0 this schema may only gain optional fields and widened enums — no field is renamed, removed, or made required — which is why `schema_version` (1.1) moves while `protocol_version` (1.0) does not. See SPEC-1.0.md §6 and §8.
$comment: The copy of this file pinned to the 1.0 freeze is published at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Narcis13/faqir-ui/v1.0.0/manifest.schema.json; the $id above tracks `main` and is the alias that always serves the newest 1.x schema. Both are byte-identical until an additive 1.x amendment lands, after which the pinned URL keeps serving the bytes 1.0 froze with — which is the whole point of pinning it. Every release tag serves the schema as that release shipped it.

changelog.note: First published as a file: component and theme manifests in one document, `changes[]` changelog entries, an `$id`, and a resolvable `$schema` on every registry manifest. Before this the contract existed only as the validator in `src/manifest.ts`.

`props` — the non-variant attributes — declared; `variants.<group>.responsive` added for the tier suffix grammar; `category` closed to a documented enum, which retired the `form` spelling in favour of `forms`.

Frozen. `schema_version` is `1.0`, `stability` and `amendment_policy` are declared in the file, this changelog is carried in it, and the schema is published at a versioned URL beside the spec. No field changed shape.

`api` — a component's controller surface, generated from the controller's `@ui:provides` annotation. Optional, so every 1.0 manifest still validates; additive under SPEC-1.0 §8. It exists because the data was already in every controller and on no surface an agent reads: `faqir explain <recipe> --json` returned no `api` for any of the 29 JS-backed recipes.

Five optional theme-manifest fields: `seed` (the generator input, absent on an authored theme), `axes` (the fourteen axes derived from the CSS, never hand-written), `fonts`, `distinctiveness` and `visual_matrix`. Optional, so every manifest written against 1.0 still validates; additive under SPEC-1.0 §8, which is why the protocol stays frozen at 1.0 while the schema moves to 1.1. The seed's vocabulary is stated in full — every axis, every enum, every default — because it is the generator's input contract, not a hint.

componentManifest.description: A primitive, recipe, pattern, or scaffold component manifest.

props.description: Attributes that are not variant groups: booleans, free-form strings and numbers read by a controller or by CSS. Consumed by the bindings codegen (framework props + defaults) and by the generated agent surfaces.

api.description: The controller's public surface — the methods `$ui` resolves to, and the object a recipe factory returns. GENERATED from the controller's own `// @ui:provides` line and its function declarations by `scripts/build-manifest-api.mjs`; never authored by hand, and checked for drift in CI. Present only on a component that ships a controller. Optional, which SPEC-1.0 §8 classifies as an additive amendment.

methods.description: Methods in the order `@ui:provides` declares them.

responsive.description: When true, every declared value is ALSO accepted as `<attr>-<tier>` for each canon breakpoint tier (sm, md, lg, xl) — `data-cols-md="6"` means "6 from the md tier up" (FAQIR-SPEC §15). Generators expand the group into per-tier props/columns automatically; the responsive grammar never applies to the five frozen protocol attributes.

prop.description: One non-variant attribute of a component: a boolean toggle, a free-form string/number, or a small enum whose values are listed but which is not a visual variant group.

name.description: Method name, exactly as `@ui:provides` lists it.

params.description: Parameter list as the controller writes it; empty for a nullary method.

description.description: First sentence of the method's JSDoc, when it has one.

category.description: The component's shelf in the registry. A closed vocabulary — the same list CONTRIBUTING.md documents. `custom` is reserved for components scaffolded by `faqir create` outside the registry.

change.description: One changelog entry (task 0.5-04). Consumed by `faqir upgrade`.

templates.description: Named HTML templates. Most components ship an `html` template; some ship only variant-specific templates (`html_group`, `html_single`, …). Every value is an HTML string.

themeManifest.description: A theme descriptor shipped as `<name>.theme.json` beside `<name>.css`. The nine required fields are schema 1.0's; the five optional ones are schema 1.1's. Two of the optional pair — `axes` and `distinctiveness` — are DERIVED from the stylesheet by a generator rather than written by hand, which is the rule `tokens_overridden` and `tokens_inherited` have followed since 0.4.

fonts.description: The self-hosted families this theme's role tokens name. Absent or empty on a theme that asks only for system faces.

visual_matrix.description: Whether this theme enters the full screenshot and axe matrix. ABSENT MEANS TRUE: a theme opts out explicitly with `false`, so a new theme is covered by default and a skipped one carries the reason in its own file (1.1A-13).

themeSeed.description: The generator input for a generated theme, written whole by `faqir theme generate` and absent on an authored theme (which has no seed). Every axis but `name` and `accent` is optional and states its own default, so `{ "name": …, "accent": … }` is a COMPLETE seed: the defaults together describe the shipped `default` theme's character, which is what makes an accent-only seed produce a theme rather than a fragment. The axis vocabulary is shared with `themeAxes` — the same fourteen axes, seen from the input side instead of the derived one.

name.description: The theme's name — the same string as the manifest's `name`. It is carried here too because the seed is also written standalone as `<name>.seed.json`, which has to be re-runnable on its own.

accent.description: Axis `accent` — the hue and chroma the primary ramp, the ring, the gradient accent and the chart palette are built from. One of the three forms the colour parser accepts: `oklch(L C H)`, a hex triplet, or `white`/`black`. The only axis with no default: a seed without an accent is not a theme.

neutral.description: Axis `neutral` — the bg / fg / border ramps' cast — `tinted` mixes the accent into the neutrals. Default `gray`.

scheme.description: Axis `scheme` — which scheme blocks the theme ships, the same vocabulary as the manifest's own `scheme`. Default `both`.

material.description: Axis `material` — which named texture `--texture-page` and `--texture-surface` point at. Default `none`.

motion.description: Axis `motion` — the `--duration-*` and `--ease-*` families (including the `linear()` springs) and `--motion-hover-lift`. Default `smooth`.

density.description: Axis `density` — the root default for the `data-density` modifier. Default `comfortable`.

contrast.description: Axis `contrast` — how far the ramps are pushed apart — `high` is the mechanism the hand-written `contrast` theme spelled out by hand. Default `standard`.

document.description: Axis `document` — whether the seed also emits the paged `<name>-document` theme beside the screen one. Default `false`.

themeAxes.description: The fourteen axes a theme actually lands on, DERIVED from its CSS by `bun run gen:theme-manifests` (1.1A-08) and never hand-written — the same rule `tokens_overridden` and `tokens_inherited` have carried since 0.4. It is the seed's vocabulary minus `accent` and `document` (an authored theme has neither) plus `accent_hue` and `accent_chroma`, because a derived accent is two numbers rather than a colour string. Every axis is present: an incomplete `axes` block is the drift the field exists to catch. Agents pick a theme by these, not by the adjectives in `mood`.

accent_hue.description: Axis `accent`, first half: the accent's OKLCH hue in degrees, read off the generated ramp. Paired with `accent_chroma` it replaces the seed's free-form `accent` string with two numbers a distance metric can subtract (1.1A-12).

accent_chroma.description: Axis `accent`, second half: the accent's OKLCH chroma. 0 is a neutral theme with no accent colour at all.

neutral.description: Axis `neutral`, read back out of the theme's CSS — the bg / fg / border ramps' cast — `tinted` mixes the accent into the neutrals.

scheme.description: Axis `scheme`, read back out of the theme's CSS — which scheme blocks the theme ships, the same vocabulary as the manifest's own `scheme`.

depth.description: Axis `depth`, read back out of the theme's CSS — the `--shadow-*` ramp, `--shadow-color` and `--surface-backdrop`.

material.description: Axis `material`, read back out of the theme's CSS — which named texture `--texture-page` and `--texture-surface` point at.

motion.description: Axis `motion`, read back out of the theme's CSS — the `--duration-*` and `--ease-*` families (including the `linear()` springs) and `--motion-hover-lift`.

density.description: Axis `density`, read back out of the theme's CSS — the root default for the `data-density` modifier.

focus.description: Axis `focus`, read back out of the theme's CSS — the `--focus-ring-*` family and `--focus-shadow`.

contrast.description: Axis `contrast`, read back out of the theme's CSS — how far the ramps are pushed apart — `high` is the mechanism the hand-written `contrast` theme spelled out by hand.

themeAxisVoice.description: Axis `type.voice` — how headings are set, independently of which family sets them. Drives `--heading-weight`, `--heading-tracking` and `--heading-transform`.

weight.description: Heading weight, resolved against the `--weight-*` ramp. Default `bold`.

tracking.description: Heading letter-spacing, added to a heading's own optical tightening. Default `normal`.

themeAxisType.description: Axis `type` — the three type decisions a theme makes: which families it pairs, how big and how far apart the ramp steps are, and how headings are voiced. Drives `--font-heading`, `--font-body`, `--font-ui`, the `--text-*` ramp and the `--heading-*` family.

pairing.description: Which families the role tokens name. `custom` means the theme states `--font-heading` and `--font-body` itself; every other value is a catalogue pairing the generator knows how to install (1.1A-18). Default `system`.

scale.description: The ratio between adjacent `--text-*` steps. Default `1.2`.

base.description: `--text-base` in CSS pixels; every other step is computed from it and the scale. Default `16`.

themeAxisShape.description: Axis `shape` — the silhouette. Drives the `--radius-*` ramp, the `--border-width-*` family and `--corner-shape`.

radius.description: How round a corner is: `sharp` is 0, `pill` is `--radius-full`, and the three between walk the `--radius-*` ramp. Default `soft`.

border.description: How heavy an edge is: `hairline` is `--border-width-sm` (today's 1px default), `regular` `-md`, `heavy` `-lg`. Default `hairline`.

corner.description: `--corner-shape` — progressive, so a browser without `corner-shape` renders `round` whatever the theme asks for. Default `round`.

themeAxisDecoration.description: Axis `decoration` — the small marks a theme makes on text and between things. Drives `--link-decoration`, `--link-underline-offset`, `--link-underline-thickness` and `--divider-style`.

link.description: How a link is underlined. `none` silences every underline in the registry at once, `offset` is today's underline with `--link-underline-offset`, `thick` leans on `--link-underline-thickness`. Default `offset`.

divider.description: `--divider-style` — the line style a separator, a divided list and a table rule draw with. Default `solid`.

themeAxisControls.description: Axis `controls` — the silhouette of the four controls a theme is recognised by. Drives the component aliases in `registry/tokens/aliases.css` (`--button-radius`, `--input-fill`, `--checkbox-radius`, `--switch-radius`, …), never a component's own stylesheet.

input.description: Text-control silhouette: a bordered `box`, a `filled` plate (`--input-fill`), or a single `underline` rule. Default `box`.

checkbox.description: Checkbox corner: `square` is `--checkbox-radius`, `round` is a circle. Default `square`.

switch.description: Switch track and thumb corner. Default `pill`.

themeFont.description: One self-hosted family a theme's role tokens name, installed by `faqir fonts add` (1.1A-18). Declared here so a project can see what a theme will download before it applies it, and so the licence travels with the theme rather than with the download.

family.description: The family name as `font-family` spells it, e.g. `Fraunces`.

license.description: The licence the family ships under, e.g. `OFL-1.1`. Faqir installs open-licensed families only; the string is what a project's own licence audit reads.

role.description: Which role token names the family.

source.description: Where the files came from — a catalogue id or a URL. Optional: a family already on the machine has no source.

themeDistinctiveness.description: How far this theme sits from the nearest other shipped theme, written by the distinctiveness gate (1.1A-12) and never by hand. It exists because 1.0 shipped twelve themes that read as one: the gate refuses a generated theme that is too close to an existing one, and this block records the measurement it refused or allowed on.

nearest.description: The name of the closest other shipped theme.

axis_distance.description: How many of the fourteen axes the two themes differ on. Two shipped themes must differ on at least four (FAQIR-VISION §5.2).

token_distance.description: Mean OKLab ΔE between the two themes' resolved colour tokens, over every scheme they both ship. The axis count says they are described differently; this says they LOOK different. The gate's floor is the same separation the framework demands between two adjacent surfaces inside one theme.
